name: LP-MSPM0C1104 LaunchPad development kit
sources: MSPM0C110x data sheet SLASF90E (rev. September 2026, read 2026-10-07: features, memories, peripherals); LaunchPad user guide SLAU908B (May 2024, read 2026-10-07: kit contents, jumpers J6 to J9 and J101, schematic header pinout J1 to J3, LED1 on PA22 for board version E3, PA4 for E2); MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07 example READMEs (pins)

columns.head: The chip: MSPM0C1104
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M0+
Runs the program, up to 24 million steps a second (24 MHz). No floating-point unit
Flash: 16 kB
Holds the program. Kept when the power is off
RAM: 1 kB
Working memory while it runs: 1,024 bytes for everything, stack included. This runs out first
Power: 3.3 V on this board
The chip accepts 1.62 to 3.6 V, so 5 V parts need care

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: up to 18 pins
Plain on/off pins: LEDs, buttons, control lines. 17 reach the 20-pin header, one of them the reset pin
UART: 1
Simple serial text. It is also the board's USB serial port, so a loop wire needs two jumpers pulled
I2C: 1 / SPI: 1
Two-wire bus for sensors / fast bus (12 Mbit/s) for displays
ADC: 1
Measures a voltage in 4,096 steps (12-bit), up to 1.5 million times a second. No DAC to make one
Timers: 3, plus a beeper
Timing and PWM; the beeper makes a 1, 2, 4 or 8 kHz tone on its own
CRC-16
Hardware checksum. No AES, no random-number hardware

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
USB debug probe (XDS110, no power meter), one red LED, user button S2, reset S1, I2C pull-ups
Headers
20 pins in two rows of female sockets (J1, J2) plus J3 for 5 V and GND. Male-ended jumpers fit
Not on the chip
No floating point, no DAC, no comparator, no AES or random numbers, no radio, no Zephyr support
Watch out
The LED pin moved between board versions (PA4 on E2, PA22 on E3). No USB cable in the box
